rows.evidence: Abstract read verbatim at nber.org/papers/t0089 and minneapolisfed.org discussion paper (same text): 'We show how to use security market data to restrict the admissible region for means and standard deviations of intertemporal marginal rates of substitution (IMRS's) of consumers. Our approach is (i) nonparametric ... (ii) characterizes the duality between the mean-standard deviation frontier for IMRS's and the familiar mean-standard deviation frontier for asset returns; and (iii) exploits the restriction that IMRS's are positive random variables.' RePEc's JPE 99(2) 225-262 page carries the same abstract content (summarised by the fetch tool, including the quoted phrase 'nonparametric and applies to a rich class of models'). The line-145 span, the line-361 span and the key-results row paraphrase exactly (i)-(iii); no extension beyond the abstract. Scope: purely methodological, no sample claim. Not a working paper; no freshness issue.

All three spans are graded T with data-locator='Abstract'. BLUEPRINT §3: T = 'proved on the page, or with a precisely cited proof'. An abstract is not a proof locator; the spans describe what the paper does (a characterization), and the on-page proofs (Theorems 2.1, 2.4) are of the page's own statements, not of the spans. The S7 calibrated ledger moved Koning (2026) from an 'Abstract' locator to a theorem locator before accepting T.
rows.fix: Either (a) give each span the JPE locator of the result it states (the section and equation numbers in JPE 99(2) where the IMRS mean-standard deviation frontier and its duality with the return frontier are derived, and where positivity is imposed), read from the paper; or (b) re-scope: make the T spans the on-page statements (Theorems 2.1/2.4, proofs on the page) and attach hansen1991implications as the source of the idea with that same section locator. rows.location: course/modules/AP/AP1/L06.html line 117 (s3 claim), line 238 (s6 claim), line 393 (key-results row 2)
rows.evidence: Original not reachable: sciencedirect.com (robots disallowed), linkinghub.elsevier.com and the Northwestern CMS-EMS DP 454 PDF (kellogg.northwestern.edu/research/math/papers/454.pdf, listed on ideas.repec.org/p/nwu/cmsems/454.html) were refused by the fetch permission system; shell curl gets proxy 403. Secondary evidence only: Schachermayer, 'The Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing' (mat.univie.ac.at/~schachermayer/preprnts/prpr0141a.pdf) states 'Theorem 1. ([15, Th. 2. 7.]) Suppose the stochastic process S = (S_t) is based on a finite, filtered, probability space ... The market model contains no arbitrage possibilities if and only if there is an equivalent martingale measure for S', [15] = Harrison-Pliska SPA 11, 215-260; the page's span copies this wording. Delbaen-Schachermayer, The Mathematics of Arbitrage (e-bookshelf sample) attributes the finite-Omega FTAP 'in its present form' to [HP 81] without a theorem number. RePEc abstract of HP81 mentions only the continuous-trading model and completeness. The locator 'Theorem 2.7' and the statement were not read in the primary source, exactly the builder's stated limitation.
rows.fix: Obtain HP81 (SPA 11(3), Section 2, the finite model) and confirm that the result numbered 2.7 states 'no arbitrage iff an equivalent martingale measure' (HP's own terms may be 'viable'/'arbitrage opportunity'); correct the locator to the printed number and page. If the original cannot be read, admit Schachermayer's survey (Encyclopedia of Quantitative Finance, Wiley, 2010) through tools/add_reference.py and cite it explicitly: data-cite='<survey key> harrison1981martingales' data-locator='Theorem 1 (citing [15, Th. 2.7])'.

rows.evidence: Read the original: Harrison & Kreps (1979), JET 20, 381-408 (sfu.ca/~kkasa/HarrisonKreps_79.pdf, found by WebSearch). Theorem 2 (p. 390) reads: 'Suppose the security price model admits no simple free lunches. Then there is a one-to-one correspondence between equivalent martingale measures P* and [continuous, strictly positive linear extensions psi of the price functional pi] ... given by P*(B) = psi(1_B) and psi(x) = E*(x)' (eq. 3.1). The strategies are self-financing SIMPLE strategies (trading at finitely many prespecified dates), not 'bounded predictable' strategies. The equivalence the page attributes to Theorem 2 (zero expected discounted gain for every strategy under a measure iff discounted prices are martingales under it) is not the theorem's statement; it appears inside the proof on p. 391 (buy one share on B in F_t at t, sell at u; price zero implies Z_k(t) = E*[Z_k(u)|F_t]) and is unnumbered. Schachermayer's survey cites '[14, Th. 2]' for this 'tantamount to a martingale' step, which is where the page's wording comes from. Attribution therefore fails at the locator: the span misstates what Theorem 2 says, and the key-results row repeats the misstatement.
rows.fix: Replace the line-237 span with: 'Harrison and Kreps's Theorem 2 (p. 390): if the price model admits no simple free lunches, equivalent martingale measures correspond one to one to the continuous, strictly positive linear extensions of the price functional; its proof (p. 391) shows that a measure gives every simple self-financing strategy zero expected discounted gain exactly when discounted prices are martingales under it.' Set data-locator='Th. 2, p. 390; proof p. 391'. Rewrite key-results row 5 the same way ('simple self-financing strategy', not 'bounded predictable strategy').

rows.location: course/modules/AP/AP1/L06.html line 362 (Problem R1 solution, first bullet)
rows.evidence: The bullet titled 'Minimal martingale or minimum-variance SDF' defines it as 'the EMM whose density is closest to one in L^2, the dynamic analogue of x*'. That is the variance-optimal (signed) martingale measure, which in general differs from Foellmer-Schweizer's minimal martingale measure (built from one-step projections). Counter-example computed in /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/6f74c4e7-484a-542c-982f-ae21506915ed/scratchpad/L05-L06/scripts/mmm_vs_vom.py: a two-period trinomial tree with a random one-step mean-variance tradeoff; the product of one-step L2 densities (minimal) has E[Z^2] = 1.072205, the global L2-closest density (variance-optimal) has E[Z^2] = 1.070875, and the densities differ by up to 0.050185, both satisfying every martingale constraint to 1e-16. The two coincide only in special cases (e.g. a deterministic mean-variance tradeoff, one period).
rows.fix: Retitle the bullet 'Variance-optimal (minimum-variance) martingale measure' and add: 'it coincides with the minimal martingale measure only when the mean-variance tradeoff is deterministic; in general they differ'. Cite registry keys for both (request Schweizer 1995/1996 and Foellmer-Schweizer 1991 through REFERENCE_REQUESTS).
